## Impact Wheel RECORD entries can contain relative paths that traverse outside of the wheel’s installation prefix. entry.title: [UPDATED] PYSEC-2026-4173: OpenStack Swift vulnerable to authenticated server-side request forgery
entry.content:
OpenStack Swift vulnerable to authenticated server-side request forgery

Aliases: CVE-2026-50221, GHSA-h8rc-w822-q8vq

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N · CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:L/SC:L/SI:L/SA:N

Affected:

  • swift — fixed in 2.37.2

In OpenStack Swift before 2.37.2, proxy-server does not strip internal update headers (X-Container-Host, X-Container-Device, X-Delete-At-Host, X-Delete-At-Device) from client requests before forwarding them to object-servers. An authenticated user with write access can inject these headers to redirect container update requests to an attacker-controlled server, enabling server-side request forgery. The SSRF requests expose internal cluster metadata including storage policy indexes, partition mappings, device names, and when at rest encryption is enabled, cipher text and initialization vectors for the container-level encryption key. The attacker can also cause "ghost listings" in arbitrary containers via the shard-range redirect mechanism.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2: certifi bundles emSign root CAs with compromised intermediate CA keys
entry.content:
certifi bundles emSign root CAs with compromised intermediate CA keys

Aliases: PYSEC-2026-4320

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • certifi — fixed in 2026.10.19

Certifi versions before 2026.10.18 include the `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root certificate in their bundled CA store. Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates that chain to this root have compromised private keys and the CA has revoked them. An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue valid-looking certificates for any hostname. If the attacker is also on-path, they can intercept or modify TLS traffic from clients that trust the certifi bundle. Examples include `requests`, `urllib3` and `pip`, and the Python.org macOS installer. Certifi 2026.10.18 removed all emSign roots from the bundle. Certifi 2026.10.19 restored the emSign roots that are not affected. Upgrade to 2026.10.19 or later, and rebuild container images that vendor certifi.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-hq85-5cpj-mr62: uv's bundled CA store trusts an emSign root whose intermediate CA keys are compromised
entry.content:
uv's bundled CA store trusts an emSign root whose intermediate CA keys are compromised

Aliases: PYSEC-2026-4321

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • uv — fixed in 0.13.4

By default, uv verifies TLS connections against a vendored copy of the `webpki-root-certs` bundle. Versions before 0.13.4 include the `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root. Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates that chain to that root have compromised private keys, and the CA has revoked them. An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue certificates that uv accepts for any hostname, and can be used to issue certificates to enable MITM attacks. uv 0.13.4 removes the root from its vendored bundle, following `webpki-root-certs` 1.0.10. Upgrade to 0.13.4 or later.
